messages:
Priya: heads-up — p95 host CPU for ingress-side preproc jumped ~18% after the 2.3.1 deploy. noticed higher latencies on short requests (<=64 tokens). flamegraph points at the sidecar tokenization + request parsing path

Maya: can you paste the perf / flamegraph output? is it on a particular region/instance-type?

Priya: ran perf on a saturated canary (c5g-large equivalent). top stacks: host_parse_request -> tokenize_pool_acquire -> writev_flush -> net_send -> kv_cache_lookup (hot eviction loop). small snippet: 

```
# perf top -p <pid>
  24.5% host_parse_request
  18.3% tokenize_pool_acquire
  12.1% writev_flush
  9.2% kv_cache_lookup
  6.0% http2_hpack_decode
```

Priya: also saw many tiny writev syscalls (4-8B payloads) instead of coalesced frames. gRPC layer shows frequent WINDOW_UPDATE churn.

Ethan: interesting. writev churn + small frames = syscall and TCP overhead. can you reproduce with ghz or wrk? try grpc bench: `ghz --proto proto/service.proto -d 1 -c 50 -n 10000 --concurrency 20` and capture tcpdump / ss stats

Priya: reproduced with ghz. baseline (2.2.9) p95 28ms, 2.3.1 p95 34ms for short requests. I captured tcpdump and see ~3x more frames.

Maya: two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer pool contention causes blocking and forces numerous small flushes; 2) new parse path changed framing order so we flush headers/body separately. Also KV cache eviction policy change in 2.3.1 could be thrashing lookups and blocking the parse thread.

Logan: what does the KV cache metric look like? hit rate, evictions/s?

Priya: metrics from last hour on canary: hit_rate dropped 4pts, evictions spiked ~1200/s. KV lookup latency median up from 0.6ms to 1.8ms.

Maya: actionable experiments:
- toggle tokenizer pool sizing back to old defaults (increase workers)
- temporarily disable the new parse flushing optimization (revert small patch)
- switch KV cache eviction from CLOCK to LRU for canary to check thrash sensitivity
- increase writev coalesce window (buffer up to 4KB before flush)

Priya: I ran a quick microbench: bumping tokenizer workers + writev coalesce -> p95 back to 29ms. KV change alone improves med latency but p95 still higher.

Ethan: can we add a short-running A/B canary with 1% traffic each for toggles? I can configure rollout in console. we should include perf traces and token-level cost.

Maya: will open a small PR with runtime flags: `--tokenizer-workers`, `--writev-coalesce-bytes`, `--kv-evict-policy`. add a feature flag so we can flip without deploy. also add a microbench harness: `scripts/ingress_latency.py --short-only`

Priya: please include perf recording command in PR description. I used: `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`. attach CPU diff and tcpdump sample.

JenkinsBot: build/redwood-runtime#3124 started: test matrix (linux-x86_64, docker).

Logan: i'll create the canary in us-west with 1% traffic, 10m ramp, and alert if p95 increases >5% vs baseline. also enable net dev stats collection (tcp_retrans, tx_queue_len) for that cohort.

Maya: quick note — for HTTP/2 we should check if HPACK decoding is now on the hot-path synchronously. if so, consider moving header decode to preparse thread to avoid blocking tokenization.

Priya: agreed. i'll capture HPACK timelines. meanwhile i'll add the flamegraphs and sample traces to the PR. thanks team.

Ethan: follow-up: can we add a synthetic test to CI that fuzzes small payloads and asserts p95 < 40ms for short token loads? that'll catch regressions earlier.

Priya: yes, adding `ingress-small-payload` benchmark to perf-suite. planning to run nightly.

JenkinsBot: build/redwood-runtime#3124 passed integration tests. deploy scheduled to canary window.

Maya: great — once canary data stabilizes we'll decide whether to keep tokenizer/work changes or tune KV heuristics further. keep notes in the PR and ping #eng-sre for watch. :thumbsup:
